items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: George Wein was, of course, the proprietor.

ctx.x: yearly places where Sarah played quite a bit. At that particular time, Storyville had been in another location, another one of those squares in Boston... It was over by the ballpark there -- I can't remember that square right now. But it had moved to Copley Square. George Wein was, of course, the proprietor. And we had had quite a few successful engagements there.

One night a fellow asked us to come out to his place. He had a place out on Route 9, I think, a club, where they closed something like 1 o'clock out there, and I think we played until about 3. But he invited us out, Sarah and the people in the group, to come out and just have free drinks and food and whatever, because he liked Sarah and he liked music. So we decided to go. We went out there. I think Sarah rode out there with Joe Benjamin, and I was with another friend of mine, a girl from New York, and I think…
